title: curmudgeon-verify Mode A dispatch gate — content-based prior-review lookup + decider-pushed-verification patched-since signal (qid 607 double no-op)

problem:
TWO independent defects in curmudgeon-verify.md's Mode A gate each would have no-op'd qid 607, and each will recur.

DEFECT 1 — filename-substring prior-review lookup. The candidate lookup is `fs.readdirSync(reviewDir).filter(f=>f.includes(item.target_id))`. Review files are frequently named by review_id/topic convention (ECLIPSE-RESPONSE-REVIEW-2026-08-17.json, PRED-batch-2026-08-14-eclipse.json), not by target_id, so the lookup returns zero candidates even when a prior review exists whose point_id field IS the target_id. Content survey of monitor/curmudgeon/reviews/ (897 parseable files): 823 carry point_id, 89 carry target_id — content-match is reliable. The 2026-08-17T15:38Z verify run hit exactly this: qid 607 target ECLIPSE-2026-08-12-GEOMETRIC-VERDICT, prior review present with matching point_id, zero filename candidates, agent correctly declined to freelance and no-op'd.

DEFECT 2 — gate (d) blind to decider self-applies. Gate (d) requires a suggested-patches-*.json with generated_at newer than the prior review's reviewed_at. The decider's self-apply path (commit db6c349, 2026-08-17: ISS-3073..3076 eclipse fixes applied directly to sections.json/generate-html.js/docs) writes NO suggested-patches file — it records via closed-issues.json + closure-ledger.jsonl + the commit itself. Newest suggested-patches at the time: 2026-08-16T02-11, older than reviewed_at 2026-08-17T01:12:31Z. So even with Defect 1 fixed, gate (d) returns false and the item still no-ops. Every future 'decider self-applies then pushes class=verification' cycle — the standard flow since PROP-081-era self-apply discipline — is structurally invisible to the verify consumer.

NET EFFECT: the verification-class consumer cannot consume the exact item class the operator re-enables it for. qid 607 drained only because MAIN curmudgeon (Opus, commit ba4030f 2026-08-18) did the verification as cycle 2 — the work happened at Opus cost on the Opus agent's single daily quiet-period slot instead of the Sonnet verify agent built for it (PROP-038's entire premise).

proposed_fix.summary: Two surgical edits to the isVerifyOwned() dispatcher block in curmudgeon-verify.md. (1) Prior-review lookup: keep the filename fast path; when it returns zero candidates, fall back to scanning review JSON contents for point_id===target_id or target_id===target_id. (2) Gate (d): treat 'this queue item was pushed by decider with class=verification after the prior review's reviewed_at' as an authoritative patched-since signal, OR'd with the existing suggested-patches file scan. No rubric changes: Check 3 iterates over whatever patch files exist (zero iterations for self-applies is safe); Checks 1/2/5 do the real content verification against the prior review's holes.

files_to_modify.find:
const candidates=fs.readdirSync(reviewDir).filter(f=>f.includes(item.target_id));
  if(candidates.length===0) return false; // no prior review → main curmudgeon's job (fresh)
files_to_modify.explanation: Defect 1 fix: content-based fallback for prior-review discovery. Lazy (only fires when filename match is empty) so no cost on conventionally-named targets. Renaming/aliasing historical review files was rejected — reviews/ is append-only (CLAUDE.md File Ownership) and the decider's own pop logic already matches by content, so the naming convention itself is not the bug.

files_to_modify.find:
const hasNewer = newerInDir(path+'/monitor/decisions') || newerInDir(path+'/monitor/decisions/applied-patches');
  if(!hasNewer) return false;
files_to_modify.explanation: Defect 2 fix: accept the decider's own class='verification' push (pushed_at > reviewed_at) as the patched-since signal. Keeps the suggested-patches scan as the fallback for legacy/manually-pushed items. Queue item schema carries pushed_by and pushed_at (verified on qid 607: pushed_by=decider, pushed_at=2026-08-17T02:17:08.664Z).

tradeoffs: GAIN: the verification-class consumer can actually consume decider-pushed verification items — the exact class the operator re-enables it for (RE-ENABLE trigger, CLAUDE.md agent table). Sonnet-cost verification instead of burning main curmudgeon's single daily Opus slot; faster drain (verify runs 3x/day when enabled vs main curmudgeon 1x/day at quiet cadence). RISK 1: content-scan parses up to ~900 review JSONs when the fast path misses — one-time ~100-200ms per queue item, only on fallback; acceptable (dispatch runs once per agent run). RISK 2: the deciderPushedVerification signal trusts the decider's push discipline — if decider ever pushes a verification item BEFORE applying fixes, verify would run against unpatched targets and report holes-not-closed; that is a self-correcting failure (the verify review would say so), not a silent one. RISK 3: broadening gate (d) slightly widens Sonnet-verify's ownership; the safety boundary is unchanged — gates (b) <=4 holes and (c) no major/critical still route adversarial work to Opus, and the in-rubric escalation hook still fires. WHAT WE LOSE: nothing structural; the old behavior is a strict subset of the new eligibility.
estimated_impact: Eliminates the recurring no-op class for topic-named reviews + self-applied patches (this was 100% of verification-class items in the current era: qid 607 is the archetype of the standard commission->review->self-apply->verify loop). Frees main-curmudgeon Opus slots from cycle-2 verification work (~$1-2/item at Opus rates vs ~$0.2-0.4 Sonnet). Removes a false 'consumer offline/broken' signal from operator re-enable decisions.
verification_pattern: grep -q 'point_id===item.target_id' monitor/prompts/curmudgeon-verify.md && grep -q 'deciderPushedVerification' monitor/prompts/curmudgeon-verify.md && echo FIXED || echo STILL_BROKEN
